items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline; a little awe on the depth reveals. Chars voices funny cartoon characters (a pompous, touchy Lake Superior; a weary deadpan Belgium), short and punchy.
lines: This one lake beats all five Great Lakes.
How does it beat all five... if it's barely bigger than Belgium?
Meet Lake By-kahl, in Siberia. The Great Lakes are not impressed.
[indignant, pompous] We're almost eight times bigger!
On a map? Sure. So where is By-kahl hiding all that water?
By-kahl plunges one thousand six hundred and forty-two metres. About four times deeper than Lake Superior.
[huffy, offended] Nobody asked you to measure.
That's nearly five Eiffel Towers deep.
But why so deep? By-kahl isn't sitting in a valley. It's filling a crack in the Earth.
Right here, the ground is slowly pulling apart.
That crack opened twenty-five to thirty million years ago. Which makes By-kahl the oldest lake on Earth.
The Great Lakes? They filled up about fourteen thousand years ago.
[embarrassed, quickly] Can we change the topic?
And the crack is still opening. About four millimetres, every year.
Width makes a lake look big... Depth makes it big.
Here's the twist. The water isn't even the bottom.
Below the lake floor lies up to seven kilometres of mud. The crack goes down about as far as Everest is tall.
And from above? It still looks barely bigger than Belgium.
[weary, deadpan sigh] Why do I keep getting dragged into this?
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
